_comment: backlog row 185. Re-run from a DETACHED clone -- bd-mutate refuses a work tree inside its own repository -- and that clone needs frontend/node_modules, because every catcher shells out to Vitest through the fail-closed bridge; a clone without it returns UNKNOWN for every mutant by construction, which must never read as a pass: git clone <candidate> /tmp/row185-clone && cp -al frontend/node_modules /tmp/row185-clone/frontend/node_modules && rm -rf /tmp/row185-clone/frontend/node_modules/.vite && venv/bin/python toolchain/bin/bd-mutate --spec tests/mutants/v3_66_1243_t8_cluster_runtime.json --work /tmp/row185-clone --timeout 300. MEASURED AGAINST THE RETIRED TEXT SCAN at base b489289: M1, M2 and M5 left the old six-assertion scan FULLY GREEN over live violations; M3, M4 and M6 it caught textually. M7 IS THE HOLE THIS CUT FOUND IN ITS OWN GATE AND CLOSED: on the first battery the new spec scored 6/6, so its UNNAMED rules were probed with eleven further mutants, and THREE escaped in succession, each invisible to the draft that had just closed the one before it. M7: a one-click fleet-wide write on a <div role=button>, outside a TAG-driven control query -- closed by making the inventory pin role/tabindex-aware and adding an exhaustive per-element sweep. M9: the same write on a PLAIN <div onMouseDown>, outside any structural selector, and fireEvent.click dispatches no mousedown. M10: the same write on a PLAIN <div onKeyDown>, which no pointer event reaches -- both closed by crossing the whole-element denominator with a REPERTOIRE of stimuli instead of one event name. Writing that sweep exposed a fourth defect in the gate itself: a synchronous loop never flushed the microtask react-query dispatches its mutationFn on, so it asserted over a queue that had not run, and was green and vacuous. That is why the sweep now carries an instrument precondition. M8 is the only OVER-CORRECTION direction: clearing the pairing token unconditionally satisfies a naive reading of the (R) write-only rule while destroying the operator's token on a transient failure, and its named control is the spec's failed-redeem retention assertion. Its preserves target reads useCluster.ts only, so it does not share the mutated Cluster.tsx path. VALIDITY CAVEAT: bd-mutate ast.parse-validates only .py and shellchecks .sh, so a .tsx/.ts mutant falls through UNVALIDATED and a malformed anchor would present as CAUGHT via an esbuild transform error rather than a real catch. Every mutant here was confirmed to fail on a SEMANTIC assertion message, never a transform error -- that is the validity evidence. All catchers share one pytest nodeid because the gate delegates to Vitest, so the catching VITEST test is named in each label.
subject: the /cluster route's runtime write-gating contract: no gated write fires from a single interaction, sync_pull cannot auto-fire on mount/focus/interval, the two A-tier writes are No-default confirmed, and the pairing token is a write-only secret cleared only on success
